DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 93 s. 2021 JUL 19 GOV. HUMERLITO A. DOLOR Office of the Provincial Governor Province of Oriental Mindoro Dear Gov. Dolor: This has reference to your letter dated 21 May 2021 requesting for an opinion on the issue of the creation of an Executive —Legislative Oversight Committee (ELOC) embedded in the general provisions of the General Appropriations Ordinance. Assailed as one of the provisions creating this Oversight Committee is as follows: "Subject to standard procurement, accounting and auditing laws, rules and regulations, no provincial funds shall be disbursed or paid by the Provincial Treasurer on account of a PGOM infrastructure project funded under this annual budget and/or any subsequent supplemental budget/s without a supporting Certificate of Inspection and full Inspection Repon by the Inspectorate Team accepting compliance with the project's plan, specifications and other requirements. The Certificate of Inspection and the Inspection Report by the Inspectorate Team shall be submitted to the Oversight Committee, the Provincial Governor, Accountant, and Treasurer, and furnished the Commission on Audit, and attached to the disbursement voucher. " Thus, specifically submitted for this Department's rendition of opinion are as follows: 2. 3. The scope and extent of delegated functions to local legislative bodies, especially during the implementation of govemment infrastructure projects, if there is any; The authority of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to amend or repeal issuances of the Local Chief Executive regarding the implementation/execution of projects, programs, and activities; The incorporation of inappropriate non-appropriation provisions creating the ELOC in the 2021 GAO, which are not germane to the title of the ordinance; and

4. The extent of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's participation in the implementation/enforcement of enacted ordinances. " We find it prudent to address the submitted issues by one comprehensive discussion so as to avoid misleading interpretations which may possibly arise if we intend to merely answer each issue "as stated". Let us start with a recall that the principle of check and balance is embodied in the constitution. This is the source of the oversight function/role of the legislature and the executive department which likewise applies at the local level given the decentralized system of our government. Simply put, it applies not only at the national level but also at the sub-national level with the office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE) and the Sanggunian being the local legislative body. It comes along with the law-making power of the Sanggunian, the veto power of the LCE and the veto-overriding power of the Sanggunian. Ideally, oversight functions ensure the interaction of the branches of the government, which in turn, guarantees responsive and accountable governance. It is for this reason that the Department supports measures that are intended to promote responsive, accountable and good local governance as it is the one in line with its mandate. The Department even implements an incentive system through the Seal of Good Local Governance (SGLG). Hence, we encourage leniency as much as both branches may tolerate, so long as the interest of the public is not prejudiced. Needless to say, the Department likewise avoids determining whether one measure already constitutes legislative or executive encroachment of the other's power — the controversy on the extent of oversight roles being a long standing debate which is rightfully to be reserved for the judiciary to determine. Going into the crux of the controversy, the matter is not plainly about exercise of oversight functions. As the creation of the Executive — Legislative Oversight Committee (ELOC) was made part of a legislative enactment, that is, the General Appropriations Ordinance, the same is protected by the presumption of validity of legislative enactments. Now, therefore, given that the creation of ELOC is part of a duly enacted ordinance, the performance of ELOC of its functions may not be deemed as encroachment by the local legislative body of the executive's implementation of government infrastructure projects, it is simply a performance by the members of the ELOC of the duties and responsibilities mandated by the ordinance.

The same may not even be considered as the Sangguniang Panlalawigan having amended or repealed issuances of the Local Chief Executive regarding the implementation/execution of projects, programs, and activities. An ordinance has the force and effect of law, and the issuances of the Local Chief Executive are made pursuant to what is mandated by the ordinance. In so far as the issue of the inclusion of alleged inappropriate provisions in an appropriation ordinance, the issues of constitutionality may be raised before the proper court. We, however, opine that the mention of the requirement on the submission of Certificate of Inspection and full Inspection Report by the Inspectorate Team is consistent with that required by R.A. 9184, otherwise known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, on the conduct of inspection by the Inspectorate Team. As to the issue of the extent of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan's participation in the implementation/enforcement of enacted ordinances, we must say that it is merely up to the exercise of oversight functions. As to the extent of this oversight function, however, we are not equipped with an authoritative yardstick to measure that extent, and we ought to reserve that to the judiciary. In DILG Opinion No. 25 s. 2020, the Department mentioned that there is no specific provision in R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", expressly granting the oversight powers to local legislative bodies. This power is only implied in the power to review the executive budget and the power of appropriation, which is still in line with ordinance enactment. This opinion is being issued without prejudice to contrary opinion/decision of competent authorities or the court. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: I NGAN Underse etary for Local Government LLLS/84 Copy furnish: DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO Regional Director, DILG-MIMAROPA 822 Quezon Avenue, Diliman, Quezon City
